00282.title: Gemcitabine + cisplatin · 28-day schedule
00282.purpose: Help control advanced urothelial cancer and its symptoms.
00282.label: Days 1, 8 and 15 · every 28 days

agents.name: Gemcitabine
agents.explanation: Gemcitabine interferes with making DNA, which dividing cancer cells need. Healthy blood-forming cells and other tissues can also be affected.
agents.watch: Report fever, unusual bleeding, breathlessness, rash, swelling or reduced urine promptly.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection, anaemia and bleeding
Nausea, vomiting, fatigue, flu-like symptoms and swelling
Rash, sore mouth and liver-test changes
Uncommon or rare serious lung inflammation, kidney injury including haemolytic uraemic syndrome, severe skin reactions and capillary leak

agents.name: Cisplatin
agents.explanation: Cisplatin forms links in DNA that interfere with copying and repair. This helps stop cancer cells dividing, but healthy tissues may also be affected. Kidney protection with fluids and monitoring is central to cisplatin treatment.
agents.watch: Report ringing in the ears, hearing changes, numbness or loss of function. Tell the team if you cannot drink, are passing less urine or become swollen or breathless during fluids.
risks: Nausea and vomiting, sometimes severe
Kidney injury and low magnesium or other electrolyte changes
Hearing loss or ringing in the ears, which may be lasting
Numbness or tingling from nerve damage, sometimes lasting
Low blood counts, serious infection and bleeding
Allergic reactions; possible fertility harm

anatomy: Call urgently for new cough or breathlessness.
Report painful sores or difficulty eating and drinking.
Blood tests check liver function; report yellow eyes or dark urine.
Follow the anti-sickness plan; call if unable to keep fluids down.
Report reduced urine or new swelling; keep kidney blood tests.
Fever, sudden illness or unusual bleeding needs urgent advice.
Report widespread rash, blistering or peeling urgently.
Report numbness, tingling, ringing ears or hearing changes.
00282.schedule: Gemcitabine is given on days 1, 8 and 15. Cisplatin is usually given after gemcitabine on day 1; the source also permits day 2. The cycle repeats every 28 days, usually for four to six cycles. Your unit confirms your actual cisplatin day and appointments.
00282.administration: Gemcitabine runs into a vein over 30 minutes. Cisplatin runs over 60 minutes with prescribed fluids before and after. Tests, pharmacy preparation, review and support medicines add to the visit time.
00282.baseline: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests; review hearing, nerves, general health, medicines and ability to receive cisplatin fluids. Hearing testing is arranged if clinically indicated.
00282.monitoring: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests on day 1; blood count and creatinine before day 8. Day-15 treatment also needs review against the intracycle count and toxicity criteria; your unit confirms the required tests. Check symptoms before every dose.
00282.support: Use one written anti-sickness plan, including medicines before treatment, tablets for home and rescue treatment. Your team reconciles steroids, interactions and any stomach-protection medicine from your local prescription. Cisplatin needs prescribed intravenous fluids and electrolyte monitoring/replacement. Follow your own fluid advice; tell the team about heart failure or fluid restriction. Review kidney function, hearing, nerves and other medicines before treatment. Gemcitabine-only days have a separate lower-risk anti-sickness plan.
00282.prep: Confirm your cisplatin day, blood-test appointments and written support prescriptions.
00282.access: Suitable intravenous access is needed. This schedule does not routinely use a take-home infusion pump.
00282.wider: This schedule is systemic treatment for advanced disease. Surgery or radiotherapy may help selected local problems; they are not automatically part of this chemotherapy calendar. Discuss the subsequent treatment or observation plan after chemotherapy.
00282.scope: This is NCCP 00282: cisplatin 70 mg/m² with gemcitabine days 1, 8 and 15 over 28 days. It is distinct from split-dose cisplatin and four-cycle upper-tract adjuvant treatment.
00282.evidence: A randomised trial in previously untreated advanced urothelial cancer compared 28-day gemcitabine/cisplatin with MVAC. Response rates were 49% and 46%; overall survival did not differ significantly (hazard ratio 1.04, 95% confidence interval 0.82–1.32).
00282.caveat: The study did not prove every GemCis schedule equivalent. It used cisplatin on day 2 and predates newer systemic options. Group averages cannot predict an individual outcome.
doses: Confirm whether cisplatin is scheduled on day 1 or day 2.
Blood counts and symptoms may change this dose.
The day-15 dose has its own safety review.

00622.schedule: Gemcitabine and cisplatin are both given on days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle, usually for four to six cycles. Cisplatin is split into two 35 mg/m² doses; do not use another GemCis calendar.
00622.administration: At each treatment visit gemcitabine runs into a vein over 30 minutes and cisplatin over 60 minutes, with prescribed fluids and support medicines. Your unit confirms visit length.
00622.baseline: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests; review hearing, nerves, other medicines and ability to receive fluids. The team must confirm whether this split-dose cisplatin plan is suitable for your kidney function.
00622.monitoring: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests on day 1; blood count and creatinine before day 8. Review symptoms, hearing, nerves, hydration and electrolytes before cisplatin.
00622.support: Use one written anti-sickness plan, including medicines before treatment, tablets for home and rescue treatment. Your team reconciles steroids, interactions and any stomach-protection medicine from your local prescription. Cisplatin needs prescribed intravenous fluids and electrolyte monitoring/replacement. Follow your own fluid advice; tell the team about heart failure or fluid restriction. Review kidney function, hearing, nerves and other medicines before treatment. Both day 1 and day 8 contain cisplatin and need their own prescribed support course.
00622.prep: Confirm two cisplatin visits per cycle and how the home anti-sickness courses fit each visit.
00622.access: Suitable intravenous access is needed. This is not a routine take-home infusion-pump schedule.
00622.wider: Treatment choice depends on kidney function, hearing, nerves, fitness and previous treatment. The source contains inconsistent renal eligibility wording, so the treating team must resolve suitability before prescribing.
00622.scope: NCCP 00622 uses cisplatin 35 mg/m² on both days 1 and 8. Its impaired-renal-function indication and CrCl <60 exclusion need clinical reconciliation; a split dose does not itself prove cisplatin is safe.
00622.evidence: Gemcitabine and cisplatin have randomised evidence in advanced urothelial cancer. The pivotal 2000 trial used a 28-day schedule with cisplatin 70 mg/m² on one day; its results provide background but do not directly establish the benefit or safety of this split-dose 21-day schedule.
00622.caveat: No response or survival percentage from the different pivotal schedule is presented as an estimate for this split-dose regimen. Treatment suitability remains an individual clinical decision.

00628.schedule: Gemcitabine is given on days 1 and 8 and cisplatin on day 1. The 21-day cycle is planned four times after surgery for eligible upper-tract urothelial cancer. Treatment may be delayed or adjusted for safety.
00628.administration: Gemcitabine runs into a vein over 30 minutes; cisplatin over 60 minutes with prescribed fluids. Review, preparation, blood tests and anti-sickness medicines add to the visit time.
00628.baseline: Review the operation and pathology, recovery and fitness within 90 days of surgery, performance status and kidney function. Full blood count, kidney and liver tests are required; review hearing, nerves, medicines and fluid tolerance.
00628.monitoring: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests on day 1; blood count and creatinine before day 8. Symptoms, hearing, nerves and hydration are reviewed before treatment.
00628.support: Use one written anti-sickness plan, including medicines before treatment, tablets for home and rescue treatment. Your team reconciles steroids, interactions and any stomach-protection medicine from your local prescription. Cisplatin needs prescribed intravenous fluids and electrolyte monitoring/replacement. Follow your own fluid advice; tell the team about heart failure or fluid restriction. Review kidney function, hearing, nerves and other medicines before treatment. Day 8 gemcitabine has a separate lower-risk anti-sickness plan.
00628.prep: Confirm the four-cycle adjuvant plan and how kidney function after surgery affects treatment selection.
00628.access: Suitable intravenous access is needed. This schedule does not routinely require a take-home infusion pump.
00628.wider: This treatment follows surgery of the upper urinary tract. It aims to treat microscopic disease that scans cannot show. Ongoing urology and oncology surveillance remains necessary; your team sets the imaging and bladder-surveillance schedule.
00628.scope: NCCP 00628 is an adjuvant upper-tract regimen for muscle-invasive and/or node-positive, non-metastatic predominantly transitional-cell disease. It is not the advanced-disease 28-day or split-dose GemCis regimen.
00628.evidence: POUT randomised 261 people after surgery for high-risk upper-tract urothelial cancer to four cycles of gemcitabine/platinum or surveillance. At five years, disease-free survival was 62% versus 45% (hazard ratio 0.55, 95% confidence interval 0.38–0.80).
00628.caveat: Disease-free survival means being alive without a recorded recurrence; it is not the same as overall survival. The trial included cisplatin or carboplatin according to kidney function, so the whole-trial result is not a cisplatin-only estimate or permission for automatic substitution.
doses: Gemcitabine only; review counts before administration.

00450.title: Mitomycin + fluorouracil with radiotherapy
00450.purpose: Support radiotherapy in treating bladder cancer while aiming to preserve the bladder in selected patients.
00450.label: Mitomycin day 1 · five-day pumps on days 1–5 and 22–26

agents.name: Mitomycin
agents.mechanism: Links DNA strands so cells cannot copy them normally
agents.explanation: Mitomycin damages the DNA that dividing cells need. With fluorouracil it helps radiotherapy act against bladder cancer. Healthy marrow and other tissues can also be affected.
agents.watch: Report fever, unusual bruising, reduced urine, breathlessness or pain around the drip promptly.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection and bleeding, which may be delayed
Nausea, mouth soreness and skin reactions
Tissue damage if the medicine leaks outside the vein
Rare serious kidney/blood-vessel injury including haemolytic uraemic syndrome
Rare serious lung inflammation; possible fertility harm

agents.name: Fluorouracil
agents.mechanism: Disrupts production of DNA and RNA
agents.explanation: Fluorouracil, often shortened to 5-FU, interferes with the building blocks used to make DNA and RNA, which cells need to grow. It runs through a vein over the prescribed hours. Dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (DPD) is an enzyme that breaks it down. Testing for DPD deficiency before treatment reduces risk but cannot rule out every severe reaction.
agents.watch: Report severe diarrhoea, mouth sores, chest pain, sudden confusion, sore palms or soles, or unexpectedly early severe symptoms.
risks: Low blood counts and serious infection
Mouth and throat soreness
Diarrhoea and dehydration
Painful palms or soles
Heart problems including chest pain
Rare severe neurological or early excessive toxicity

anatomy: New breathlessness or cough needs urgent assessment.
Report painful mouth ulcers, especially if you cannot drink.
Chest pain, breathlessness or faintness needs emergency assessment.
Report diarrhoea early; severe pain or dehydration needs urgent help.
Report reduced urine, blood in urine or painful urination.
Fever, sudden illness or unusual bleeding needs urgent advice.
Report painful palms/soles, rash or pain/swelling around the intravenous line.
Sudden confusion, unsteadiness or severe unexpected symptoms need urgent help.
00450.schedule: Mitomycin is given once on day 1. Fluorouracil runs continuously through a pump over 120 hours on days 1–5 and again on days 22–26, alongside the prescribed radiotherapy course. This is one chemoradiation course, not a repeating 28-day chemotherapy cycle.
00450.administration: Mitomycin is given through a carefully checked intravenous line. Each fluorouracil pump provides 500 mg/m² per day for five days, a total of 2500 mg/m² over 120 hours. The unit arranges pump connection, disconnection and line care.
00450.baseline: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests. Confirm dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (DPD) testing before first fluorouracil unless previously tested. Review the heart history, medicines, intravenous access and radiotherapy plan.
00450.monitoring: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests weekly. Review mouth, bowel, skin, urinary and cardiac symptoms and the pump/line. Additional tests depend on symptoms or abnormal results.
00450.support: Use one written anti-sickness plan, including medicines before treatment, tablets for home and rescue treatment. Your team reconciles steroids, interactions and any stomach-protection medicine from your local prescription. Ask for a written mouth-care and diarrhoea plan, pump contacts and line-care instructions. Stomach protection and other local adjuncts should be reconciled with the actual prescription.
00450.prep: Confirm the DPD result, pump training, connection/disconnection appointments and the radiotherapy department’s bladder-preparation instructions.
00450.access: A suitable central line and ambulatory pump are usually used for the continuous fluorouracil infusions. Call the unit immediately about leaking, disconnection, alarms, redness, pain or swelling; never change the infusion rate yourself.
00450.wider: Radiotherapy treats the bladder locally while chemotherapy makes cancer cells more sensitive to it. The radiation oncology team specifies dose, fractions and preparation. Follow-up bladder examinations are essential, and surgery may still be required if treatment does not control the cancer.
00450.scope: NCCP 00450 is the bladder chemoradiation schedule with five-day fluorouracil infusions. Radiotherapy fractions and appointments are prescribed separately; the timeline is an educational reference.
00450.evidence: In BC2001, 360 people were randomised to bladder radiotherapy with or without fluorouracil and mitomycin. Two-year freedom from locoregional disease was 67% with chemoradiation versus 54% with radiotherapy alone (hazard ratio 0.68, 95% confidence interval 0.48–0.96).
00450.caveat: This demonstrates improved local control compared with radiotherapy alone; it does not prove superiority to bladder-removal surgery. Overall survival was not significantly different in the primary report. Suitability for bladder preservation requires multidisciplinary assessment.

00759.schedule: Gemcitabine 100 mg/m² is given weekly on days 1, 8, 15 and 22, two to four hours before radiotherapy. There are four planned gemcitabine doses in one course. This low-dose schedule is different from gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² chemotherapy.

00759.baseline: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests; review fitness, current medicines and the radiotherapy plan.
00759.monitoring: Full blood count weekly; kidney and liver tests at the end of the course as specified in the regimen, with extra testing if clinically required. Review bowel, urinary, skin, breathing and general symptoms during treatment.

00759.access: Suitable intravenous access is needed for the weekly infusion. This schedule does not routinely use a take-home pump.

00759.scope: NCCP 00759 is four weekly 100 mg/m² gemcitabine doses with radiotherapy. Do not import a 1000 mg/m² gemcitabine dose, repeated chemotherapy cycles or another radiotherapy prescription.
00759.evidence: GemX was a single-arm phase II study of 50 people with muscle-invasive bladder cancer. Forty-four patients, 88% of the study group, had a complete response at the bladder examination after treatment.

00333.schedule: Methotrexate is given on day 1; vinblastine, doxorubicin and cisplatin on day 2. The cycle repeats every 14 days. Granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) is prescribed on days 3–7. The consultant sets total treatment duration; no fixed four- or six-cycle course is implied.
00333.monitoring: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests before each cycle; review symptoms, infection, bowel function, hearing, nerves and fluid balance. Review cardiac symptoms and cumulative doxorubicin exposure.
00333.wider: NCCP 00333 covers advanced/metastatic disease with performance status 0–1. A perioperative dose-dense MVAC plan requires its own explicit multidisciplinary prescribing context; it is not inferred from this page.
00333.scope: This is the 14-day MVAC schedule with G-CSF. It must not be confused with 28-day MVAC or three-drug CMV.
00333.evidence: In 263 patients with advanced urothelial cancer, dose-dense MVAC with G-CSF was compared with conventional MVAC. Complete responses were 21% versus 9%; median progression-free survival was 9.1 versus 8.2 months (hazard ratio 0.75, 95% confidence interval 0.58–0.98).
00333.caveat: The initial report did not show a statistically significant overall-survival difference. These advanced-disease findings do not establish the benefit of a perioperative course. A response is not the same as cure.

00337.monitoring: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests before each cycle; blood count and kidney tests before day 8. Review mouth, bowel, hydration, infection, hearing, nerves and folinic-acid use.
00337.wider: The multidisciplinary team plans the surgery or other definitive local treatment and recovery interval. Chemotherapy does not replace that local treatment. Follow-up remains necessary after completion.
00337.scope: The NCCP body specifies 21-day CMV; a 14-day footer label conflicts with it. The prescribing team must reconcile that source error. This schedule has no doxorubicin and requires folinic-acid rescue.
00337.evidence: The BA06 trial compared three cycles of CMV before local treatment with local treatment alone. At ten years, overall survival was 36% versus 30% (hazard ratio 0.84, 95% confidence interval 0.72–0.99).
00337.caveat: The benefit was measured across trial groups receiving definitive local treatment. It does not mean that chemotherapy alone is curative or predict an individual outcome.
doses: Confirm folinic-acid rescue for the following day.
Cisplatin over 120 minutes with hydration; folinic acid starts 24 hours after methotrexate.
Blood and kidney checks before the dose.
Start 24 hours after day-8 methotrexate; four doses six hours apart.

00338.administration: Treatment is given intravenously. Methotrexate and vinblastine are short administrations; where used, doxorubicin is given through carefully checked access. Cisplatin requires prescribed hydration and a longer visit. The team confirms exact administration and observation times.
00338.baseline: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests, ECG, review of hearing, nerves, bowel function, medicines and any fluid collections. Hearing testing is arranged when indicated. Doxorubicin schedules need cardiac assessment and echocardiogram/MUGA if over 65 or clinically indicated, with lifetime anthracycline exposure reviewed.
00338.support: Use one written anti-sickness plan, including medicines before treatment, tablets for home and rescue treatment. Your team reconciles steroids, interactions and any stomach-protection medicine from your local prescription. Cisplatin needs prescribed intravenous fluids and electrolyte monitoring/replacement. Follow your own fluid advice; tell the team about heart failure or fluid restriction. Review kidney function, hearing, nerves and other medicines before treatment. Methotrexate interacts with several medicines, including some antibiotics, anti-inflammatory painkillers and proton-pump inhibitors. Do not start, stop or combine medicines without oncology/pharmacy advice. The aprepitant–vinblastine interaction also requires pharmacy reconciliation.
00338.access: Suitable intravenous access is essential. Vinblastine and doxorubicin can damage tissue if they leak; report burning, pain or swelling immediately. No routine take-home infusion pump is part of these schedules.
00338.prep: Confirm each treatment day, blood-test appointments, support medicines and any growth-factor or folinic-acid prescription.
00338.title: MVAC · 28-day schedule
00338.context: Urothelial cancer · treatment intent must be specified
00338.purpose: Treat urothelial cancer before surgery, after surgery, or in advanced disease according to the prescribed indication.
00338.label: Days 1, 2, 15 and 22 · every 28 days

agents.name: Methotrexate
agents.explanation: Methotrexate interferes with folate-dependent reactions that cells need to make DNA. This can slow cancer-cell division, while also affecting blood-cell production and the lining of the mouth and bowel.
agents.watch: Tell the pharmacist about all painkillers, antibiotics, supplements and other medicines because interactions can increase methotrexate toxicity. Report new cough or breathlessness, mouth ulcers, unusual bleeding, jaundice, reduced urine or severe rash promptly.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection, anaemia and bleeding
Mouth ulcers, nausea, diarrhoea and liver-test changes
Kidney injury or slower drug clearance with kidney impairment, dehydration, interacting medicines or fluid collections
Uncommon serious lung inflammation, severe skin reactions and liver injury; fertility and pregnancy harm

agents.name: Vinblastine
agents.explanation: Vinblastine prevents cells from separating normally when they divide. It can also affect blood cells, nerves and bowel movement.
agents.watch: Report constipation, abdominal swelling, numbness or pain around the drip.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection and bleeding
Constipation, sometimes severe bowel blockage or paralysis
Numbness, tingling or weakness from nerve injury
Mouth soreness, nausea and hair loss
Tissue injury if drug leaks outside the vein; fertility and pregnancy harm

agents.name: Doxorubicin
agents.mechanism: Damages DNA and interferes with repair
agents.explanation: Doxorubicin interacts with DNA and topoisomerase II, disrupting copying and repair. Its heart and tissue effects require particular care.
agents.watch: Follow the unit’s cisplatin hydration plan and individual fluid target. The source advises 2–3 litres on Day 1 to reduce bladder irritation from cyclophosphamide; the team must adapt this if heart or kidney problems restrict fluids. Report blood in urine or painful urination promptly.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection, anaemia and bleeding
Nausea, vomiting, mouth soreness and hair loss
Heart muscle damage, sometimes delayed or permanent; risk depends on lifetime exposure and other factors
Tissue injury if drug leaks outside the vein
Temporary red urine after the dose; report painful or persistent red urine
Rare later blood cancer; fertility and pregnancy harm

agents.name: Cisplatin
agents.explanation: Cisplatin forms links in DNA that interfere with copying and repair. This helps stop cancer cells dividing, but healthy tissues may also be affected. Kidney protection with fluids and monitoring is central to cisplatin treatment.
agents.watch: Report ringing in the ears, hearing changes, numbness or loss of function. Tell the team if you cannot drink, are passing less urine or become swollen or breathless during fluids.
risks: Nausea and vomiting, sometimes severe
Kidney injury and low magnesium or other electrolyte changes
Hearing loss or ringing in the ears, which may be lasting
Numbness or tingling from nerve damage, sometimes lasting
Low blood counts, serious infection and bleeding
Allergic reactions; possible fertility harm

anatomy: Report new cough or breathlessness urgently.
Report painful ulcers or difficulty drinking.
Chest pain, palpitations, swelling or breathlessness needs urgent advice.
Report constipation early; severe pain, swelling or vomiting needs urgent help.
Report reduced urine, ringing ears or hearing changes; tests guide dosing.
Fever, sudden illness or unusual bleeding needs urgent advice.
Tell the nurse immediately about pain, burning or swelling around the drip.
Report numbness, tingling, weakness or balance changes before the next dose.
00338.schedule: Methotrexate is given on days 1, 15 and 22; vinblastine on days 2, 15 and 22; doxorubicin and cisplatin on day 2. The cycle repeats every 28 days. NCCP specifies three cycles before surgery, four after surgery, or up to six in metastatic disease; your team records which applies.
00338.monitoring: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests before each cycle; blood count and kidney tests before days 15 and 22. Review infection, mouth, bowel, hearing, nerves, cardiac symptoms and cumulative doxorubicin exposure.
00338.wider: For a preoperative course, surgery remains part of the plan. An adjuvant course follows surgery to reduce recurrence risk. Advanced-disease treatment aims at disease and symptom control. These settings have different goals, durations and follow-up.
00338.scope: This is conventional 28-day MVAC, not the 14-day G-CSF-supported schedule. Do not copy its cycle count, G-CSF timing or day-15/day-22 appointments into another regimen.
00338.evidence: SWOG 8710 compared three cycles of MVAC followed by bladder-removal surgery with surgery alone. Median overall survival was 77 versus 46 months; the two-sided survival comparison had P=0.06. No residual cancer at surgery was found in 38% versus 15%.
00338.caveat: The survival comparison did not meet the conventional two-sided 0.05 threshold. These results concern neoadjuvant treatment followed by surgery and must not be presented as an adjuvant or metastatic benefit estimate.
doses: Blood count and kidney tests before treatment.
Blood count and kidney tests before treatment.

00583.title: Pembrolizumab + axitinib
00583.context: Advanced clear-cell-component kidney cancer · first line
00583.purpose: Help control advanced kidney cancer using immunotherapy and a blood-vessel-growth inhibitor.
00583.label: Pembrolizumab every 21 days · axitinib twice daily

agents.name: Pembrolizumab
agents.explanation: Pembrolizumab blocks PD-1, a signal that can limit the activity of immune cells. This can help them attack cancer, but can also cause inflammation in healthy organs during treatment or after it ends.
agents.watch: Report new diarrhoea, cough, breathlessness, rash, headache, unusual weakness, thirst or changes in urine promptly.
risks: Immune inflammation can affect the lungs, bowel, liver, kidneys, skin, eyes, heart, muscles or nervous system and can be severe or fatal
Hormone-gland inflammation can affect the thyroid, pituitary or adrenal glands; diabetes can occur and hormone replacement may be lifelong
Severe skin reactions, including blistering or peeling; infusion reactions
Immune effects can start during treatment or months after stopping; tell every healthcare professional about immunotherapy

agents.name: Axitinib
agents.type: Targeted therapy: VEGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor
agents.mechanism: Axitinib blocks vascular endothelial growth factor receptors (VEGFRs), signals that help tumours grow new blood vessels. Reducing this blood supply can slow cancer growth. The same action explains effects on blood pressure, kidneys, bleeding and wound healing.
agents.explanation: Axitinib blocks vascular endothelial growth factor receptors (VEGFRs), signals that help tumours grow new blood vessels. Reducing this blood supply can slow cancer growth. The same action explains effects on blood pressure, kidneys, bleeding and wound healing.
risks: High blood pressure, sometimes severe; rare heart failure, heart attack, stroke or clots
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, constipation, reduced appetite and weight loss
Sore mouth, taste changes, fatigue and voice changes
Painful, red or peeling palms and soles; rash and dry skin
Thyroid changes, liver-test abnormalities and protein in the urine
Bleeding, occasionally serious; rare bowel perforation or abnormal connections (fistulas)
Delayed wound healing; rare reversible brain swelling syndrome (PRES)
Anaemia and changes in other blood cells; possible fertility and pregnancy harm
agents.watch: Collect a prescription for diarrhoea medicine, usually loperamide, before starting. Follow the supplied instructions and contact the team for persistent diarrhoea, dizziness, poor intake or reduced urine.

anatomy: New cough or breathlessness may mean immune inflammation; call urgently.
Report severe tiredness, dizziness, headache, thirst or frequent urination.
Monitor blood pressure; chest pain, collapse or stroke symptoms need emergency help.
Report diarrhoea early; blood, severe pain or persistent diarrhoea needs urgent review.
Tests monitor the liver; report yellow eyes, dark urine or severe nausea.
Report reduced urine, swelling or blood in urine; protein may need testing.
Report painful palms/soles, widespread rash, blistering or peeling.
Severe headache, confusion, seizures, weakness or vision change needs emergency help.
00583.schedule: Pembrolizumab 200 mg is given intravenously every 21 days. Axitinib starts at 5 mg twice daily, about 12 hours apart, continuously, with or without food. Only your team may change the dose. Do not take an extra axitinib dose after a missed or vomited dose. Duration depends on benefit, tolerance and the agreed plan.
00583.administration: Pembrolizumab runs over 30 minutes with observation according to local policy. Swallow axitinib tablets whole with water; follow the prescribed twice-daily dose and pharmacy instructions.
00583.baseline: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests, glucose, thyroid tests, blood pressure and ECG. Review autoimmune conditions, previous treatment, medicines, bleeding, wound healing and endocrine symptoms.
00583.monitoring: Review blood pressure, blood count, kidney and liver tests, glucose and thyroid function regularly. The team specifies dates and any home blood-pressure record. ECG, cortisol and other tests are added when indicated. Review diarrhoea, breathing, rash, fatigue and endocrine symptoms before each infusion.
00583.support: Routine anti-sickness prophylaxis is not usually required; use the individual symptom plan. Bring an immunotherapy alert card. Follow blood-pressure treatment, skin/foot care and the diarrhoea plan. Steroids for suspected immune toxicity require medical direction. Review CYP3A-interacting medicines, grapefruit and herbal products with pharmacy.
00583.prep: Confirm infusion appointments, daily tablet dose, home blood-pressure instructions and urgent contact numbers.
00583.access: Pembrolizumab needs suitable intravenous access. Axitinib is taken at home; no infusion pump is used.
00583.wider: This NCCP combination is first-line treatment for advanced RCC with a clear-cell component. Treatment after progression, surgery or radiotherapy for selected problems is agreed individually. Ongoing hormone replacement may be needed after an immune effect, even after treatment stops.
00583.scope: Pembrolizumab is held or stopped for toxicity, never dose-reduced. Axitinib has separate dose levels and holding rules. Liver injury or diarrhoea can involve either medicine, so do not attribute symptoms or change tablets without advice.
00583.evidence: KEYNOTE-426 randomised 861 people to pembrolizumab/axitinib or sunitinib. In the first interim analysis, 12-month overall survival was 89.9% versus 78.3%; median progression-free survival was 15.1 versus 11.1 months.
00583.caveat: These are the dated initial trial results, not a personalised prognosis or the latest follow-up. The trial compared with sunitinib, not every current first-line combination. Its treatment-duration rules do not automatically define the NCCP prescription.
doses: Take the prescribed twice-daily dose continuously, including between infusion visits.

00846.title: Enfortumab vedotin · monotherapy
00846.context: Advanced urothelial cancer · after platinum and immunotherapy
00846.purpose: Help control advanced urothelial cancer previously treated with platinum chemotherapy and a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor.
00846.label: Days 1, 8 and 15 · every 28 days

agents.name: Enfortumab vedotin
agents.mechanism: Delivers a cell-division inhibitor to cells bearing nectin-4
agents.explanation: An antibody attaches to a protein called nectin-4 and delivers a chemotherapy payload that disrupts cell division. Healthy skin, nerves and other tissues can also be affected. This is not a checkpoint immunotherapy medicine.
agents.watch: Report any rash early, especially blistering, fever or mouth/eye/genital sores; also report thirst, frequent urination, numbness or new breathing symptoms.
risks: Skin rash, sometimes severe or life-threatening including Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis; serious reactions may occur in the first cycle
High blood glucose and diabetic ketoacidosis, including in people without known diabetes
Numbness, tingling or weakness from peripheral neuropathy, sometimes lasting
Dry eyes, blurred vision and corneal problems
Lung inflammation, sometimes severe or fatal
Low blood counts, serious infection, anaemia and bleeding
Fatigue, reduced appetite, taste changes, nausea, diarrhoea and hair loss
Infusion reactions and tissue injury from leakage outside the vein; fertility and pregnancy harm

anatomy: New cough, fever or breathlessness needs urgent assessment.
Report blurred vision, eye pain, dry eyes or mouth sores.
Thirst, frequent urine, vomiting, confusion or deep breathing needs urgent help.
Report persistent diarrhoea, poor intake or difficulty drinking.
Report reduced urine or inability to keep fluids down.
Fever, sudden illness or unusual bleeding needs urgent advice.
Report any rash early; blistering, peeling or fever with rash needs urgent help.
Report numbness, tingling, weakness or balance problems before the next dose.
00846.schedule: Enfortumab vedotin is given on days 1, 8 and 15 of a 28-day cycle. The starting dose is 1.25 mg/kg, capped at 125 mg per dose. The team may hold, reduce or stop treatment for side effects. Treatment continues while appropriate according to benefit and tolerance.
00846.administration: The infusion runs over 30 minutes through a carefully checked intravenous line. Tests, review and observation add to the visit time. Tell the nurse immediately if there is pain or swelling around the line.
00846.baseline: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests, glucose, HbA1c and lipase; review diabetes, skin, nerve symptoms and current medicines. Eye assessment is arranged if indicated.
00846.monitoring: Blood count, kidney/liver tests and glucose on days 1, 8 and 15 in cycle 1, then on day 1 of later cycles in the NCCP schedule, with additional tests as clinically needed. Lipase and HbA1c on day 1 if indicated. Review skin and nerve symptoms throughout; assess eye or breathing symptoms promptly.
00846.support: Follow the prescribed low-risk anti-sickness plan. Ask about moisturiser, skin care and artificial tears for dry eyes. Check glucose as directed, including if not previously diabetic. Premedication with an antihistamine, antipyretic and intravenous steroid is considered for subsequent infusions after a prior infusion reaction; it is not an automatic routine prescription for everyone.
00846.prep: Confirm diabetes/glucose advice, a skin and eye-care plan, baseline nerve symptoms and contact numbers.
00846.access: Suitable intravenous access is needed. There is no routine take-home pump. Report pain, redness or swelling around the infusion site immediately.
00846.wider: This page covers enfortumab alone after prior platinum and checkpoint immunotherapy. It is distinct from first-line enfortumab plus pembrolizumab, which has a different schedule and risk context.
00846.scope: Severe skin reactions may occur early, including the first cycle. High glucose, lung inflammation, neuropathy and eye problems need prompt assessment; a week without an infusion is not a guaranteed symptom-free week.
00846.evidence: EV-301 randomised 608 people previously treated with platinum and a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor. Median overall survival was 12.88 months with enfortumab versus 8.97 months with investigator-selected chemotherapy (hazard ratio 0.70, 95% confidence interval 0.56–0.89).
00846.caveat: These group medians do not predict an individual lifespan. The result concerns later-line monotherapy and must not be substituted for evidence about first-line enfortumab/pembrolizumab.
doses: Review skin, glucose, nerves and other symptoms before treatment.
Review skin, glucose, nerves and other symptoms before treatment.
Review skin, glucose, nerves and other symptoms before treatment.
